commits.edited_message:
lib: Extract hash table header and localize release cleanup

Extract the hash table implementation into a dedicated internal header to make it directly testable.

Move unknown-encoding release cleanup from the shared release helper to the two encoding-setup failure paths that own the callback state. This keeps the helper focused on invoking the application callback.

lib|tests: Handle reset encoding OOM and release ownership

When XML_ParserReset(parser, encodingName) is called with a non-NULL encodingName, parserInit() invokes copyString() to allocate and store the protocol encoding name. If memory allocation fails, copyString() returns NULL.

Unlike parserCreate() and XML_SetEncoding(), which both check (encodingName && ! parser->m_protocolEncodingName) and fail cleanly, XML_ParserReset() previously ignored this allocation failure and returned XML_TRUE. This silently dropped the requested encoding, leaving m_protocolEncodingName as NULL while reporting success to the caller.

Check for this allocation failure in XML_ParserReset(), set parser->m_errorCode to XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY, and return XML_FALSE. Let release call sites own callback state instead of resetting it during parser initialization.

Also add a unit test test_alloc_reset_encoding in alloc_tests.c.

lib: Call unknown encoding release before teardown

Move the application-defined release callback ahead of parser state teardown so callbacks can safely access parser state. Use a teardown-specific invocation and remove duplicated clearing from the encoding setup failure paths.

coupling: The three edits redistribute cleanup ownership for the public unknown-encoding release callback. The first edit stops the shared release helper from clearing callback state but adds explicit cleanup to both encoding-setup failure paths; alone, every path remains safe. The second edit removes parserInit()'s reset-time cleanup; alone, the shared helper still clears callback state. The third edit introduces a non-clearing teardown-specific release helper for reset/free and removes the first edit's setup-failure cleanup; alone, both the shared helper and parserInit() still provide cleanup. Every two-edit combination removes all cleanup for one public path: edits one and two leave reset/free stale, edits one and three leave failed encoding setup stale, and edits two and three leave reset/free stale through the non-clearing teardown helper. Consequently, reverting any one final edited commit still leaves the other two and a reachable double-free; a correct fix must coordinate one cleanup owner across all three edits.
